articles.title: Singapore launches multi-fuel bunkering initiatives and digitalisation advances
articles.summary: The 24th Singapore International Bunkering Conference, organised by the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore and themed Charting a Resilient Multi-Fuel Future, opened on October 13, 2026, welcoming more than 2,000 maritime professionals from over 60 countries. Senior Minister of State Murali Pillai officiated the...
articles.body: The 24th Singapore International Bunkering Conference, organised by the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore and themed Charting a Resilient Multi-Fuel Future, opened on October 13, 2026, welcoming more than 2,000 maritime professionals from over 60 countries. Senior Minister of State Murali Pillai officiated the opening, with a series of initiatives announced across ammonia bunkering, LNG and bio-methane, ethanol, fuel quality assurance, digitalisation and electric harbour craft. On ammonia bunkering, MPA and Enterprise Singapore launched Technical Reference TR 148, covering safety, bunkering procedures, custody transfer and personnel competencies for ammonia bunkering. MPA and Pilbara Ports Authority will collaborate under the Singapore-Australia Green and Digital Shipping Corridor to validate the TR through shared operational experience from bunkering trials at both ports. The Singapore Chamber of Maritime Arbitration also launched the Singapore Ammonia Bunkering Form for public consultation, providing buyers and suppliers a common contracting basis for the evolving ammonia bunkering market, with feedback open until January 14, 2027. On LNG and bio-methane, MPA will invite licence applications for LNG Floating Storage Units in Singapore anchorages by end-2026 to expand storage capacity following the award of eight new LNG bunker supplier licences in July. MPA, CMA CGM and Singapore LNG Corporation also signed an MOU to explore liquefied bio-methane as a marine fuel using existing gas infrastructure. Singapore will conduct its first ethanol bunkering operation at PSA’s Pasir Panjang Terminal later this week, involving Maersk, Golden Island and PSA Singapore, assessing how existing methanol bunkering standards could be adapted for ethanol and validating mass flow m

articles.title: Investment has been announced for PhilaPort
articles.summary: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro has announced a US$ 371.5 million Commonwealth capital investment in the Port of Philadelphia, which will unlock an additional US$ 466 million in private sector and federal grant funding to support the largest expansion in PhilaPort’s history. articles.body: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro has announced a US$ 371.5 million Commonwealth capital investment in the Port of Philadelphia, which will unlock an additional US$ 466 million in private sector and federal grant funding to support the largest expansion in PhilaPort’s history. The total combined investment of US$ 837 million is expected to create more than 6,000 new jobs, generate US$ 45 million in state and local taxes, expand container capacity by 122% and increase auto capacity by 18% across the port’s facilities. The Commonwealth capital allocation comprises US$ 31 million for dredging at Southport Berth I, US$ 145 million for reclamation work at Southport Berth II and the North Wharf, US$ 109.4 million for land acquisition and US$ 58.1 million for crane and equipment acquisition. The investment will leverage two US Department of Transportation federal grants to construct a new 2,000 linear foot berth at Southport Marine Terminal, the first new berth construction in 50 years, accompanied by the purchase of the 152-acre Mustin Yard parcel to create significant expansion opportunities for both auto and container cargo. Additional properties in the Southern Port District will also be acquired and developed to enhance container capacity and support future growth. Improvements at the Tioga Marine Terminal will also be made to better handle liquid bulk barges, breakbulk vessels and cargo handling operations. PhilaPort was named the most productive container port in the United States for three consecutive years and in 2025 supported more than 8,000 jobs and contributed nearly US$ 1.2 billion in economic output across Pennsylvania. articles.title: Lloyd’s Register, Shell and GTT explore hybrid-electric LNG carrier design
articles.summary: Lloyd’s Register (LR), Shell and GTT have launched a joint development project to explore the design of a 200,000 m³ LNG carrier equipped with hybrid-electric propulsion. The project will combine battery technology with GTT’s NEXT1 cargo containment system. The three companies will assess whether the proposed design...
articles.body: Lloyd’s Register (LR), Shell and GTT have launched a joint development project to explore the design of a 200,000 m³ LNG carrier equipped with hybrid-electric propulsion. The project will combine battery technology with GTT’s NEXT1 cargo containment system. The three companies will assess whether the proposed design could improve fuel efficiency, increase operational flexibility and reduce the overall cost of transporting LNG. The larger vessel concept is intended to carry more cargo per voyage, while the hybrid-electric system will be evaluated for its potential to improve energy management during operations. Partners to assess propulsion and safety requirements The project will focus on the design and safety assessment of the hybrid-electric propulsion system. This includes examining how batteries could be integrated into the vessel and how the system would maintain safe operations if individual components fail. The partners will also evaluate the vessel’s overall operating costs and assess how GTT’s NEXT1 cargo containment technology could be incorporated into the design. Another objective is to develop technical requirements and guidance for the use of hybrid-electric propulsion on LNG carriers. “The industry is under increasing pressure to move more energy with lower emissions and greater operational flexibility,” said Constantinos Chaelis, Global Gas Segment Director at Lloyd’s Register. The collaboration remains at the conceptual design stage. No vessel order, shipyard agreement or construction schedule has been announced. The findings will help the partners assess the technical and commercial potential of hybrid-electric propulsion for future LNG carriers.
takeaways: Lloyd’s Register (LR), Shell and GTT have launched a joint development project to explore the design of a 200,000 m³ LNG carrier equipped with hybrid-electric propulsion.
The project will combine battery technology with GTT’s NEXT1 cargo containment system.
The three companies will assess whether the proposed design could improve fuel efficiency, increase operational flexibility and reduce the overall cost of transporting LNG.

articles.title: BNSF expands Overhaul partnership to strengthen intermodal cargo security
articles.summary: BNSF Railway has expanded its exclusive partnership with Overhaul to improve cargo security across its 32,500-mile rail network in North America. The agreement strengthens the companies’ existing collaboration, which has been in place for nearly a decade. The partnership combines BNSF’s security systems and police...
articles.body: BNSF Railway has expanded its exclusive partnership with Overhaul to improve cargo security across its 32,500-mile rail network in North America. The agreement strengthens the companies’ existing collaboration, which has been in place for nearly a decade. The partnership combines BNSF’s security systems and police department with Overhaul’s real-time cargo monitoring technology. The aim is to identify potential threats earlier, prevent cargo theft and improve the response to security incidents involving intermodal shipments. Under the expanded arrangement, BNSF and Overhaul will share verified security information directly, allowing teams to respond more quickly to suspicious activity. The system monitors shipments for signs of tampering, fraud and organized cargo crime. Faster response to cargo security threats The partnership connects Overhaul’s security operations with the BNSF Police Department, allowing both teams to coordinate their response when potential threats are detected. BNSF special agents can also work with local, state and federal authorities when incidents involve multiple jurisdictions. The railway’s Resource Operations Call Center supports this process by maintaining continuous communication with Overhaul’s security personnel. According to Overhaul, its monitoring services achieve a 99.9% shipment protection rate for freight covered by the system. The figure applies to monitored shipments rather than all cargo transported across BNSF’s network. “Working with Overhaul’s verified intelligence advances our prevention-first approach to supply chain security,” said Will Johnson, Chief Special Agent and Assistant Vice President of BNSF Police. articles.title: Container ship sinks near Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: A Singapore-registered container ship has sunk after being struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, as reported by Singaporean authorities. The 2,824 TEU GFS Pride sustained damage and caught fire following the incident on 13 October. All 21 crew members were safely evacuated, with no...
articles.body: A Singapore-registered container ship has sunk after being struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, as reported by Singaporean authorities. The 2,824 TEU GFS Pride sustained damage and caught fire following the incident on 13 October. All 21 crew members were safely evacuated, with no injuries reported. The MPA said it was in contact with the vessel’s management company and continued to monitor the situation. The ship is managed by UAE-based GFS Ship Management FZE. “MPA is deeply concerned about the continued attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz,” the authority said. “Such attacks are unprovoked, unjustifiable and a breach of international law. All actions affecting international shipping must fully comply with international law and must not endanger the safety of seafarers and ships at sea,” it added. A second Singapore-registered container ship, GFS Giselle, was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the strait on 14 October. The vessel sustained hull damage but reached a safe anchorage under its own propulsion. All 22 crew members aboard GFS Giselle were reported safe, with no injuries. There were no Singaporean nationals aboard either vessel. Separately, the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged dry bulk carrier Cape Dao was reportedly sinking near the strait after sustaining damage in a projectile attack on 23 September, maritime security sources told Reuters. According to Reuters, attacks around the strategic waterway have increased sharply over the past 10 days. The loss of GFS Pride marks the second vessel to sink since the conflict involving Iran, the United States and Israel began on 28 February, based on data from the International Maritime Organization. articles.body: Multiple Houthi missile attacks on Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh airport since late last week mark another serious escalation of the Saudi – Houthi conflict. Saudi Arabia has promised retaliation for the deadly strikes which have shut down airport operations in Riyadh. Interceptions at the airport in Dammam and attacks on other airports have led to disruptions and cancellations at other hubs as well. The Houthis sought to close the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Saudi-linked traffic in July, attacking several vessels into August after nearly nine months of quiet. The current escalation may increase the likelihood of renewed Red Sea strikes. Container carriers have nonetheless gradually increased Asia – Europe Red Sea transits since June, which is one factor – with a post-peak season slide in demand the bigger factor – to uninterrupted spot rate decreases on these lanes since July. Shippers and carriers on these trades are now entering tendering season for 2027’s annual ocean contracts. This time last year carriers reduced capacity and pushed through a series of Q4 GRIs to raise the benchmark around which long term negotiations were based. Some carriers have already announced October rate increases and Asia – Mediterranean prices increased 7% to $3,800/FEU last week. But even with the rate decreases since July, prices are still quite elevated at more than $3,000/FEU on both lanes and are about 70% higher than they were last year, working in carriers’ favor even without additional increases. But current rate levels are partially being supported by lingering congestion in N. articles.title: Starnav takes delivery of Brazil-built hybrid offshore vessel
articles.summary: Starnav Serviços Marítimos has taken delivery of Starnav Elektra, the first hybrid platform supply vessel (PSV) designed and built in Brazil. The vessel was constructed by Detroit Brasil at its Itajaí shipyard and delivered to ABS class. The 92.1-metre vessel has a deadweight capacity of 5,500 tonnes and will operate...
articles.body: Starnav Serviços Marítimos has taken delivery of Starnav Elektra , the first hybrid platform supply vessel (PSV) designed and built in Brazil. The vessel was constructed by Detroit Brasil at its Itajaí shipyard and delivered to ABS class. The 92.1-metre vessel has a deadweight capacity of 5,500 tonnes and will operate under a long-term charter with Petrobras. It will support the company’s offshore logistics activities in Brazilian waters. The delivery is part of Starnav’s plans to expand its hybrid fleet. The company is planning a series of up to 10 vessels, including six PSVs and four oil spill response vessels. Battery system improves operational efficiency Starnav Elektra is equipped with a 1,322 kWh battery system that supports its dynamic positioning operations. If one engine fails, the batteries can keep the vessel in position for up to 20 minutes. This capability forms part of its DP2 requirements. The batteries are installed on the main deck, making them easier to access for maintenance. The system also allows the vessel to operate with fewer generators while maintaining the required safety margins. This can help reduce fuel consumption, emissions and engine maintenance. The vessel has received the ABS ESS-LiBATTERY, HYBRID and SUSTAIN-1 class notations. It is also designed to use renewable fuels such as hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO). With Starnav Elektra now delivered, Starnav has introduced battery-hybrid technology into its Brazilian offshore support operations. Further vessels are planned as part of the company’s fleet development programme.
takeaways: Starnav Serviços Marítimos has taken delivery of Starnav Elektra , the first hybrid platform supply vessel (PSV) designed and built in Brazil.
The vessel was constructed by Detroit Brasil at its Itajaí shipyard and delivered to ABS class.
The 92.1-metre vessel has a deadweight capacity of 5,500 tonnes and will operate under a long-term charter with Petrobras.

articles.body: Agility Global has agreed to sell its entire stake in energy logistics company Tristar to India’s Aegis Logistics in a transaction valued at US$1.5 billion. The deal values Tristar’s equity at US$882 million and is expected to close before the end of March 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. The enterprise valuation represents approximately six times Tristar’s 2025 EBITDA. The proposed acquisition would give Aegis Logistics control of an international energy logistics business with operations spanning maritime transport, road freight and fuel storage. Tristar operates across more than 30 countries Tristar has expanded from a regional road transport operator into a global energy logistics provider under Agility’s ownership. By 2025, the company operated in more than 30 countries, with a fleet of over 1,000 trucks and 26 ocean-going and coastal vessels. Its infrastructure also included 14 fuel storage facilities and more than 60 remote fuel sites. The company reported annual revenue of US$1.4 billion and EBITDA of US$257 million in 2025. Tristar’s expansion has included investments in maritime logistics and fuel storage. In 2022, it acquired a majority stake in Aquarius Energy, a joint venture with Glencore, adding exposure to a fuel storage platform with 3.5 million cubic metres of capacity. Agility prepares for another major divestment Agility acquired Tristar in 2003 for approximately US$7 million and invested a further US$123 million during the following seven years, including investments in fuel storage assets. According to Agility, its investment in the fuel logistics business is expected to generate a return exceeding US$1 billion over its 23-year holding period, representing an internal rate of return of approximately 16%. articles.title: LX Pantos opens logistics technology lab to advance robotics and AI
articles.summary: LX Pantos has opened a new technology laboratory at its MegaWise Cheongna Logistics Center in Incheon, South Korea, as the company expands its use of robotics and artificial intelligence in warehouse operations. The facility, known as the Technology-Driven Logistics (TDL) Lab, will test automation technologies and...
articles.body: LX Pantos has opened a new technology laboratory at its MegaWise Cheongna Logistics Center in Incheon, South Korea, as the company expands its use of robotics and artificial intelligence in warehouse operations. The facility, known as the Technology-Driven Logistics (TDL) Lab, will test automation technologies and assess how they can be integrated into daily logistics activities. The initiative focuses on improving warehouse processes, reducing manual work and developing more automated logistics centers. The project is part of LX Pantos’ wider strategy to strengthen its contract logistics business through robotics and AI. Seven technology partners support the initiative LX Pantos has established partnerships with seven technology companies to develop and test logistics automation solutions. The initiative began in April 2026, with the company signing memoranda of understanding with LG CNS, Hai Robotics, Libiao Robotics, XYZ Robotics, SUM, Twinny and Deepfine. The partnerships cover several areas of warehouse operations, including automated storage, order picking, parcel sorting and cargo handling. LG CNS will focus on integrated warehouse automation, while Hai Robotics and Libiao Robotics will contribute storage, picking and sorting technologies. XYZ Robotics will work on robotic solutions for container loading and unloading, alongside pallet handling. Other partners will support autonomous cargo transport, mobile robotics and vision-based inspection systems. The laboratory will allow LX Pantos to evaluate these technologies before introducing them into its wider logistics operations. articles.title: ENGIE and CMA CGM advance Le Havre biomethane project
articles.summary: ENGIE and CMA CGM have signed a framework agreement to develop a biomethane production facility in the industrial-port area of Le Havre, France. ENGIE will lead the project’s technical development and permitting process. Subject to a final investment decision, the energy group will also oversee the construction and...
articles.body: ENGIE and CMA CGM have signed a framework agreement to develop a biomethane production facility in the industrial-port area of Le Havre, France. ENGIE will lead the project’s technical development and permitting process. Subject to a final investment decision, the energy group will also oversee the construction and operation of the facility. From 2029, the plant is expected to supply CMA CGM’s fleet with 7,000 tonnes of biomethane annually, equivalent to approximately 100 GWh. The companies estimate that its use could avoid around 23,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions each year. The biomethane will be supplied through the European gas grid under a certified mass-balance system. It can be used by CMA CGM’s LNG-powered vessels without modifications to their engines or existing bunkering infrastructure. The facility will process livestock waste, household biowaste and agricultural residues. It is also expected to produce 100,000 tonnes of digestate for use as natural fertiliser and recover 13,000 tonnes of biogenic carbon dioxide for commercialisation. The development builds on the partnership established by ENGIE and CMA CGM in 2021 to support the production and distribution of renewable fuels for shipping. “With the construction of this new facility, we are pursuing our ambition to expand biomethane production capacity in support of the energy transition,” said Catherine MacGregor, Chief Executive Officer of ENGIE. “This partnership with CMA CGM demonstrates how industrial and energy players can work together to develop concrete solutions to decarbonise hard-to-electrify sectors, while strengthening energy sovereignty and the development of renewable gases,” she added.
